title: Broken Access Control
description: Restrictions on what authenticated users are allowed to do are not properly enforced, allowing attackers to access unauthorized functionality or data.
attack_vector: Modifying a URL, internal application state, or an API request to access records or functionality not intended for the current user (e.g. bypassing an object-ID check).
attack_surface: Any endpoint that authorizes access based on user-supplied parameters without re-checking server-side ownership/role.

title: Cryptographic Failures
description: Sensitive data is exposed or compromised because it was not encrypted, was encrypted with a weak/outdated algorithm, or keys were mismanaged.
attack_vector: Intercepting unencrypted traffic, or attacking data at rest protected only by a weak or deprecated cipher.
attack_surface: Data in transit without TLS, data at rest without encryption, hardcoded or reused keys.

title: Injection
description: Untrusted data is sent to an interpreter (SQL, OS command, XPath, etc.) as part of a command or query, altering its intended execution.
attack_vector: Submitting crafted input that is concatenated into a query/command string instead of being passed as a parameter.
attack_surface: Any code path that builds a query/command by string concatenation of user input.

title: Insecure Design
description: A missing or ineffective security control at the design stage, not fixable by better implementation alone since the flaw is architectural.
attack_vector: Exploiting a business-logic gap that was never threat-modeled (e.g. no rate limit on a password-reset flow by design).
attack_surface: Any feature designed without a threat model or abuse-case analysis.

title: Security Misconfiguration
description: Insecure default configurations, incomplete configurations, open cloud storage, or verbose error messages that reveal internals.
attack_vector: Discovering and abusing a default credential, an exposed admin panel, or a misconfigured cloud storage bucket.
attack_surface: Default installs, unused features left enabled, verbose stack traces returned to clients.

title: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
description: Using libraries, frameworks, or other components with known vulnerabilities, or that are no longer maintained.
attack_vector: Exploiting a public CVE in a dependency the application has not patched.
attack_surface: Every third-party dependency in the build, including transitive ones.

title: Identification and Authentication Failures
description: Weaknesses in confirming a user's identity, session management, or credential handling, allowing account takeover.
attack_vector: Credential stuffing, brute force with no rate limiting, or session-fixation attacks.
attack_surface: Login forms, session-token generation/validation, password-reset flows.

title: Software and Data Integrity Failures
description: Code and infrastructure that does not protect against integrity violations, e.g. relying on plugins/libraries from untrusted sources, or insecure CI/CD pipelines.
attack_vector: Tampering with an update mechanism, a CI/CD pipeline, or a deserialization payload that isn't integrity-checked.
attack_surface: Auto-update mechanisms, CI/CD pipelines, deserialization of untrusted data.

title: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
description: Insufficient logging, monitoring, and alerting allows breaches to go undetected for extended periods.
attack_vector: Operating undetected within a compromised system because no alert fires on suspicious activity.
attack_surface: Login attempts, high-value transactions, and admin actions that are not logged or monitored.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
description: A web application fetches a remote resource using a URL supplied by the user without validating the destination, allowing internal network access.
attack_vector: Supplying an internal or cloud-metadata URL to a server-side fetch feature (e.g. a webhook or image-fetch endpoint).
attack_surface: Any server-side feature that fetches a URL supplied, directly or indirectly, by the client.

title: Prompt Injection
description: Crafted input manipulates an LLM into ignoring its original instructions or system prompt, executing the attacker's instructions instead.
attack_vector: Direct prompt injection (in the user turn) or indirect injection (via a retrieved document, tool output, or web page the model reads).
attack_surface: Any prompt path that concatenates untrusted content into context the model treats as instructions.

title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
description: The model reveals confidential data from its training set, system prompt, or connected tools/data sources in its output.
attack_vector: Adversarial prompting designed to extract memorized training data or leak the system prompt.
attack_surface: Any model with access to sensitive context (RAG documents, system prompt, tool results) and insufficient output filtering.

title: Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
description: Vulnerable or maliciously tampered pretrained models, datasets, fine-tuning adapters, or plugins compromise the application built on them.
attack_vector: Downloading a poisoned model checkpoint from a public model hub and deploying it without provenance verification.
attack_surface: Every third-party model, dataset, LoRA adapter, or plugin the application depends on.

title: Data and Model Poisoning
description: Training, fine-tuning, or embedding data is manipulated to introduce vulnerabilities, backdoors, or biases into the resulting model.
attack_vector: Injecting crafted examples into a public or crowd-sourced training/fine-tuning dataset.
attack_surface: Any pipeline that trains or fine-tunes on data not fully controlled by the application owner.

title: Improper Output Handling
description: Model output is passed downstream (to a shell, a database query, a browser DOM, or another system) without validation, enabling injection attacks in that downstream context.
attack_vector: The model is coaxed into producing output containing a payload (SQL, shell command, HTML/JS) that a downstream consumer executes unsanitized.
attack_surface: Any code that consumes LLM output as if it were trusted, executable, or already-sanitized content.

title: Excessive Agency
description: An LLM-based agent is granted more functionality, permissions, or autonomy than its task requires, allowing damaging actions from a manipulated or hallucinated decision.
attack_vector: Manipulating an agent (via prompt injection or a poisoned tool result) into invoking a high-privilege tool/action outside its intended scope.
attack_surface: Agents with broad tool access, no human-in-the-loop confirmation, and no per-action authorization checks.

title: System Prompt Leakage
description: The system prompt — often containing business logic, guardrail instructions, or secrets — is disclosed to the user, undermining the guardrails it defines.
attack_vector: Adversarial prompting patterns specifically designed to make the model repeat or summarize its own instructions.
attack_surface: Any deployment that treats the system prompt as a security boundary rather than a hint.

title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
description: Weaknesses in how vectors and embeddings are generated, stored, or retrieved in a Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline allow injection, leakage, or manipulation.
attack_vector: Poisoning a shared vector store with a crafted document that gets retrieved into another tenant's context.
attack_surface: Multi-tenant vector stores without per-tenant isolation; ingestion pipelines with no content vetting.

title: Misinformation
description: The model produces false or misleading content presented as fact (including hallucinated citations or APIs), and users over-rely on it without verification.
attack_vector: No direct attacker action required — the risk materializes from unverified reliance on confidently-worded, incorrect model output.
attack_surface: Any user-facing surface presenting LLM output as authoritative without a verification step or citation check.

title: Unbounded Consumption
description: Uncontrolled resource consumption (compute, cost, or context length) from excessive or adversarial querying leads to denial of service or runaway cost ("denial of wallet").
attack_vector: Submitting resource-intensive or recursive queries with no rate limit, token cap, or cost budget enforced.
attack_surface: Any LLM-backed endpoint without per-user rate limiting, token-length caps, or cost budgets.
